labels.label: rem:pushup

hypotheses.paper: future causal / chronological curves and their concatenation (l.1375)
hypotheses.note: CausalCurveOn, ChronalCurveOn of Causal.Curves (DEC-6), concatenation CurveOn.concat
PushUp quantifies over every open U; PushUpOn W for every open W as well

findings: ETT.tex:1375–1376: the first sentence is false at κ = 0 as well, for the concatenated curve itself. Take the axis segment [−1, 0] ending at a BTZ point p, a future causal curve (E0.axis_causalCurveOn), and follow it by any future chronal curve from p (one exists: e0_exists_chronalCurveOn). The concatenation is a future causal curve that is not chronal, because its points at −1 and 0 both lie on the axis and nothing is ≪ a point of the axis (pushup_concat_counterexample, e0_concat_not_chronal). The 'Equivalently' at l.1376 therefore joins a false sentence to the true inclusions. The wording finding recorded for κ > 0 holds at κ = 0, with a Lean witness here; the inclusions (push-up, every open set, future and past) are proved.

The first sentence is read literally with DEC-6's curves: the concatenated curve is itself a future chronal curve (ChronalCurveOn). The other reading, 'the end points of the concatenation are chronologically related', is push-up, and it is proved.

labels.label: lem:densite_modele

hypotheses.note: p ∉ E0.axis; e0_Jminus_axis_ne_closure_Iminus shows the restriction is necessary

hypotheses.paper: a causally convex open subset V, with J^± and I^± taken in V
hypotheses.note: CausallyConvexIn V ⊤, V open; J^±_V, I^±_V; closure in V read as closure(·) ∩ V, the reading of the strict massive_densite_of_causallyConvexIn

hypotheses.paper: [brunswic2021cauchy, §1.2]: J^±(p) is the closure of its interior (cited in the proof)
hypotheses.note: not used; true for J⁺ everywhere and for J⁻ off the axis, false for J⁻ at BTZ points (proved)

findings: ETT.tex:1480–1482: the cited fact 'for every p the set J^±(p) is the closure of its interior' is false for J⁻(p) at a BTZ point of E₀. There J⁻(p) is the half-line {r = 0, τ ≤ τ(p)}, with empty interior (e0_Jminus_axis_ne_closure_interior). The fact holds for J⁺(p) at every point and for J⁻(p) off the axis (e0_Jplus_eq_closure_interior, e0_Jminus_eq_closure_interior).

ETT.tex:1482: the condition 'if p ∈ Z^∓(E_κ)' does not match the argument. lem:IJ_calc needs no condition on p, and the closure step needs J^±(p) to be the closure of its interior, which holds for J⁺ at every p and for J⁻ when p ∉ sing₀. The condition the argument needs is p ∈ Z^±(E_κ). As printed, the condition for J⁻ is p ∈ Z⁺ = E₀, which admits BTZ points, and there J⁻(p) ≠ closure I⁻(p) = ∅ (e0_Jminus_axis_ne_closure_Iminus). Statement (b) excludes these points, so it is the proof that overreaches. With p ∈ Z^±, the main argument also covers (a) at BTZ points.

ETT.tex:1488–1491: (a) at a BTZ point is argued from I⁺(p) = reg(J⁺(p)) (defi:causal_E0, l.1353–1355). That identity is false at every BTZ point (DEC-64; Causal.E0.Iplus_ne_Jplus_diff). (a) is still true there: e0_densite_a proves it directly from push-up and Z⁺ = E₀, and the main argument with the condition corrected to p ∈ Z^± also gives it, so the paragraph can go.

ETT.tex:1480–1481: at κ = 0 the citation is not needed either. (a) and (b) follow from push-up, Z⁺ = E₀, Z⁻ = reg(E₀) and the closedness of J^±(p). For (b) one more step is needed when J⁻(p) contains axis points q: the axis points just below q are ≪ p when p is regular (E0.lt_axis_iff), and they tend to q.

(c) is read with the closure in E₀ and sing(E₀) = E0.axis.
